summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against every clause of the supplied Greek working source. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the conditional blessing, emphatic prohibition against wavering, promised strengthening, assertion that repentance without following the commandments is vain, and subsequent commands and promises. The rendering of δυναταί is contextually defensible and its alternative is disclosed. Bracketed “all” remains distinguished from unbracketed text, matching the source’s editorial marking. Repentance terminology follows current contextual policy without adding a doctrinal condition. This acceptance concerns the supplied text and disclosures only; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify the named edition, or establish a unique interpretation.
